items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the private housing finance law, in relation to residential emergency services to offer home repairs to the elderly program
items.lawCode: Add Art 28 §§1233 - 1235, Priv Hous Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2253

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the private housing finance law, in relation to
residential emergency services to offer home repairs to the elderly
program

 PURPOSE :

This bill establishes the Residential Emergency Services to Offer
(Home) Repairs to the Elderly Program to provide financial resources
to assist senior citizen homeowners with the cost of addressing
emergencies and code violations that pose a threat to their health and
safety, or affecting the livability of their home.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one provides for creation of the Residential Emergency
Services to Offer (Home) Repairs to the Elderly (RESTORE) Program and
sets forth definitions. Within the funding available, units of local
government and eligible not-for-profit organizations with experience
in housing and community development activities, may apply to the
Housing Trust Fund Corporation to administer local RESTORE programs.
Program contracts may not exceed $500,000 and must be completed within
three years, with the provision for two additional one year
extensions. Municipalities and not-for-profit organizations serving as
local program administrators shall be entitled to a 7.5%
administrative fee.

Eligible senior homeowners, age sixty and over, with an annual
household income of less than 100% of area median income may apply
through local RESTORE programs for emergency home repair services.
Local program administrators administering the RESTORE program must
respond and inspect eligible properties within 72-hours; qualified
repairs must be commenced within seven calendar days and completed
within thirty calendar days of the start of the repairs, unless
otherwise determined by the agency. The total amount of repairs may
not exceed $10,000.

Section two provides that this act shall take effect on the one
hundred eightieth day after it shall have become law.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The enacted 2016-17 budget appropriated $1.4 million for the Housing
Opportunities Program for the Elderly. This program assists senior
citizen homeowners with the cost of addressing emergencies and code
violations that pose a threat to their health and safety, or affecting
the livability of their home. It is administered by the Division of
Housing and Community Renewal (DHCR) and Housing Trust Fund
Corporation, as the Residential Emergency Services to Offer (Home)
Repairs to the Elderly (RESTORE) Program.

Over the last seventeen years, nearly $9 million in resources have
been allocated for the RESTORE program through the Division of Housing
and Community Renewal's budget appropriation. In response to growing
need and increased program demand, the annual appropriation for this
program has more than tripled in the last two fiscal years.  This bill
recognizes the importance of the RESTORE program in addressing
emergency home repairs for seniors, by providing for its permanency in
statute. It also ensures that program requirements remain consistent
and responsive to local needs, while also providing greater
predictability for the municipalities and not-for-profit organizations
serving as local program administrators.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: S7828-A Passed Senate

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None. The enacted FY 2016-17 budget appropriated $1.4 million within
DHCR's Capital Projects budget for the Housing Opportunities Program
for the Elderly. This program is operated as the Residential Emergency
Services to Offer (Home) Repairs to the Elderly (RESTORE) Program.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become law.
